new_scholarship.description: The Short-term Program (PE) of the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan lets young PhD holders and PhD researchers conduct collaborative research in Japan for between 1 and 12 months. It is restricted to candidates from the United States, Canada, EU member states, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway and Russia, who hold a doctoral degree obtained within the previous six years or are currently enrolled in a doctoral course abroad. JSPS runs three open-call rounds a year and awards 20 fellowships per round. The maintenance allowance is JPY 362,000 per month for PhD holders and JPY 200,000 for non-PhD holders, on top of a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance.

programme_detail_official.description: The Short-term Program (PE) of the Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan was started in 1997 under a domestic recruitment system run twice, later three times, a year. It provides young PhD students and PhD researchers in eligible countries with opportunities to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of Japanese hosts for between 1 and 12 months. Twenty fellowships are awarded in each FY2027 round. Financial support comprises a maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month for PhD holders and JPY 200,000 for non-PhD holders, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY 200,000 and overseas travel insurance.

programme_detail_official.description: The JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan exist to strengthen overseas researchers' research activities while advancing science and promoting internationalisation in Japan. The programme consists of a Long-term option for long-term collaborative research visits and a Short-term option for visits of 14 to 60 days for discussions, opinion exchanges and lectures. Grantees are selected after a Japanese host researcher submits an invitation application through the head of their university or institution. The maintenance allowance is JPY 387,600 per month, with a round-trip economy air ticket, overseas travel insurance and a host-applied research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000.

Meet the world.' - this is the official Study in NL / Nuffic mark and was chosen. (2) The programme lockup 'Logo NL Scholarship' (/sites/default/files/styles/page_header_logo/public/2023-07/NL%20Scholarship%20logo%20RGB.jpg?itok=xZnehePN) probed 200 image/jpeg at 7,142 bytes but pixel analysis on a white canvas found 0.0% dark pixels against 79.7% light, so it is effectively invisible on a light card and was rejected under the white-on-light rule. (3) /themes/custom/nuffic_sih_theme/src/svg/nl-sticker.svg probed 200 image/svg+xml at 1,397 bytes but its alt is 'NL Platform logo', a different organisation's mark, so it was rejected as a provenance error. Note on attribution: the NL Scholarship is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science plus 11 research universities and 24 universities of applied sciences, and no consolidated ministry or consortium mark exists on the record's own domain; using any single participating university's logo would be a provenance error. The Study in NL / Nuffic mark is used instead because Nuffic administers the scholarship, owns studyinnl.org, and that is the body recorded as official_source.
